facts.fact: 她走到村里，几乎认不出来
facts.anchor: When I reached the village, I barely recognised it.

facts.fact: 每道排水沟、每根路灯都挂着鲜艳的粉彩三角旗，在路面和人行道上投下飘动的影子；每家咖啡馆、餐馆、酒馆门口都堆着半边莲和三色堇的桶，浓烈的花香呛在喉咙后头
facts.anchor: Bright pastel bunting hung from every gutter and every lamppost, casting fluttering shadows over the road and pavements.

facts.fact: 每扇窗都装上荷叶边格子布窗帘，每张桌子都铺着波点可擦桌布——"像贺曼频道在这地方吐了一地"；没有泥，草都一样齐，鹅卵石干净得过分
facts.anchor: It was as if the Hallmark channel had thrown up all over the place.

facts.fact: 装饰极端到"所有被暗示出的温馨都被烧掉了"，只剩一片粉彩塑料的单一种植园；这让想起迪士尼乐园、扮装角色、她当年很擅长写的那种品牌邮件
facts.anchor: It was so extreme that all inferred cosiness had been burned away and all that was left was a monoculture of pastel plastic.

facts.fact: 过 Bodach's Brig 桥时，她看见咖啡馆的 Maggie 假笑全没了，正拿扫帚敲咖啡馆窗边七只吊篮中的一只，边敲边皱眉；少年们不见踪影；村里很安静
facts.anchor: As I crossed Bodach’s Brig, I saw Maggie from Maggie’s Café, all pretence of a smile gone now, trying to knock down one of the seven hanging baskets clustered around the café windows with a broom, and scowling as she did.

facts.fact: 她盯着那份"咄咄逼人的欢快"装饰：花缠满每根路灯，直到看不见灯柱；花盆花槽把路弄得几乎走不通；她想笑，觉得这确实可笑，却笑不出来
facts.anchor: I stared at the aggressively cheery decoration.

facts.fact: 不只是那种威胁感、那层体面薄漆下真正失控的东西——"还有别的。某种悲伤的东西。"
facts.anchor: It wasn’t just the feeling of threat underlying it all, the thin veneer of respectability over something truly unhinged. There was something else.

facts.fact: 她用没伤的手去碰 Maggie 打落到地上的一只花篮：里面是小小的、娇嫩的水仙，花瓣白得几乎透明，喇叭口是阳光般的黄；花瓣在指间又冷又软
facts.anchor: The petals were cold and soft in my fingers.

facts.fact: 她想："可怜的小东西。你本该让人愉快，可你只是在把所有人吓跑。"
facts.anchor: Poor wee thing, I thought. You’re supposed to be cheerful, but you’re just frightening everyone away.

facts.fact: 她直起身：该把这事查到底，趁疯劲还没蔓延到整个村子
facts.anchor: It was time I got to the bottom of this, before the madness spread across the whole village.

facts.fact: 她穿过一排向日葵、拐进通往 The Curtyard 的小巷，走进酒馆，发现村里大多数人缩在里面
facts.anchor: I stepped inside the pub and found most of the other villagers hunkering within.

facts.fact: 门一响，所有人跳起来转身，像她戳破了一只气球；地方挤满人却静得诡异，没人说话比耳语大声
facts.anchor: Everyone jumped and turned to the sound of the door as if I’d popped a balloon. The place was packed and yet eerily quiet. No one spoke louder than a whisper.

facts.fact: Viv 站在吧台后盯着波纹玻璃窗，阳光的粉彩色在她 T 恤上一列斑马上跳动；阳台上的斑马们似乎在不满地旁观
facts.anchor: Viv stood behind the bar staring toward the rippled windows, the light from the sunny pastel colours dancing over the zebras marching across her T-shirt.

facts.fact: 她唯一没看到的脸是 Rowan 的（她想象他在上面的树间、坐在幼树丛里看云从谷上过来）和那个老头子的
facts.anchor: The only faces I couldn’t see were Rowan’s—I imagined he was up among the trees, sat among the saplings, watching the clouds come over the glen—and the old man’s.

facts.fact: 之前那个男孩说："看，狗女人来了。"——这一次没人笑
facts.anchor: “Look. The dog woman’s arrived,” said the boy from earlier.

facts.fact: Dave 朝男孩那边瞪眼："闭嘴。"男孩缩回卡座里皱眉
facts.anchor: “Shut up.” Dave glowered in the boy’s direction. The boy sank down in the booth and scowled.

facts.fact: Viv 在打电话，低声而愤怒地问什么时候有人能来"把那片丛林砍下来"；架子上那排斑马似乎往后缩
facts.anchor: She was on her phone, speaking in low, angry tones about when someone could come out to “hack the jungle down”.

facts.fact: 她问"打扰一下，我在找——"，Viv 没从窗上移开视线，指了指房间另一头："嗯，壁炉旁边那道门。"
facts.anchor: “Yeah, through the door by the fireplace.”

facts.fact: 壁炉旁果然有一道门，她以前从没见过那儿有门；也许是个私人餐室
facts.anchor: Sure enough, there was a door next to the fireplace. I’d never seen a door there before.

facts.fact: Viv 说："她说要留意你。"——当然，她在等她
facts.anchor: “She said to keep an eye out for you.”

facts.fact: 她穿过人群走到门边，溜了进去
facts.anchor: I shuffled through the crowd to the door and slipped inside.
